title: Free module sheaves only depend on the sheafification of the presheaf of sets
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] and $R$ a ring. For a presheaf of sets $P$ on $\mathcal C$ let $R[P]$ be the presheaf of $R$-modules $U\mapsto R[P(U)]$, the free $R$-module on the set $P(U)$ [def-weil-pbc-free-module], with restriction along $V\to U$ the $R$-linear map sending a basis element $[x]$ to $[x|_V]$; a morphism $u:P\to Q$ of presheaves of sets induces $R[u]:R[P]\to R[Q]$, $[x]\mapsto[u(x)]$. Let $u:P\to Q$ be a morphism of presheaves of sets whose sheafification $u^\#:P^\#\to Q^\#$ (as presheaves of sets) [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] is an isomorphism. Then the sheafification $R[u]^\#:R[P]^\#\to R[Q]^\#$ (as presheaves of $R$-modules) is an isomorphism of sheaves of $R$-modules.

source.place: Hypercoverings, Section Tag 01GA (label section-acyclicity), lines 545-566: F -> Z_F is left adjoint to the forgetful functor and 'the functor F -> Z_F^# is a left adjoint as well'; Sites, Proposition Tag 00WH (label proposition-sheafification-adjoint); for R-modules the same adjunction F -> R[F]^#; by adjunction Hom(R[P]^#, M) = Hom_PSh(P, M) = Hom_Sh(P^#, M) for every sheaf of R-modules M (whose underlying presheaf of sets is a sheaf), so R[u]^# is an isomorphism by Yoneda.
